bank.prompt: When Brisbane City Council planned to rename West Nundah in 1941, which name was first proposed before the wartime choice was settled on?
bank.reveal: Plans for a post-war suburb initially nominated 'Beverley Hills', but a morale-boosting wartime name was chosen instead — Wavell Heights, honouring General Archibald Wavell, commander of Allied forces in the Middle East in 1940–41.

source.title: Pfingst Farmhouse | Heritage Places

bank.prompt: What was the suburb of Wavell Heights called before it was renamed in 1941?
bank.reveal: Renamed Wavell Heights in 1941, the suburb had been known as West Nundah — and residents on Hillcrest Avenue had variously considered their street part of Kedron, West Nundah, and Chermside.

bank.prompt: Brisbane's very first tram tracks, laid in 1884, ran between which two points?
bank.reveal: In 1884 the privately owned Metropolitan Tramway and Investment Company laid six and a half miles of track from Woolloongabba to Breakfast Creek, with branches to the Exhibition Building and New Farm.

bank.prompt: During World War I, Brisbane's 1880s New Farm mansion 'Strathmore' at 840 Brunswick Street served what wartime function from 1916–1918?
bank.reveal: The grand 1880s masonry dwelling originally known as 'Strathmore' — built for Palace Hotel proprietor David Lyons — served as Incholm Private Hospital from 1916–1918, before becoming a boarding house by the late 1930s.
